1.explanation: The CMake grammar definition lives in src/languages/cmake.js, where comment patterns are declared. Currently it only defines single-line comments starting with '#'. The special CMake block comment syntax using '#[[' to begin and ']]' to end is not included. To fix the issue, src/languages/cmake.js must be updated to add a multi-line comment rule matching '#\[\[' ... '\]\]'.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting CMake code with highlight.js, the multi-line comment syntax #[[ ... ]] is not recognized as a block comment. Instead, highlight.js treats the opening '#[[' as a single-line comment marker and does not gray out the enclosed lines. This causes the interior of the supposed block comment to render as regular code rather than as a comment, as shown in the provided screenshot.

2.explanation: The CMake language definition lives in src/languages/cmake.js. It currently only recognizes single-line comments starting with “#” and lacks any rule for the CMake-style block comments delimited by “#[[” and “]]”. To support multi-line comments, this file must be updated to include a begin/end pattern (e.g. begin: /#\[\[/, end: /\]\]/) so that highlight.js can correctly match and style entire comment blocks.
2.bug_scenario: When using highlight.js to render CMake code, multi-line comments delimited by “#[[” and “]]” are not recognized correctly. Instead of greying out all lines between these delimiters, only the first line is treated as a single-line comment (“# …”), and the closing “]]” is left as plain text.
